finding.claim: The /mirror endpoint fetches a user-supplied URL after a host check that is too weak. The check uses endswith('example.com') with no leading dot, so any domain that merely ends in those characters passes (e.g. attackerexample.com, or evil.com.example.com on an attacker-owned zone). The constant ALLOWED_SUFFIX = '.example.com' is defined but never used. An attacker can register such a domain and point its DNS at an internal address such as 169.254.169.254, 127.0.0.1 or an RFC1918 host. The server then requests that internal address, and the response length is returned. Scheme and port are not restricted, and the resolved IP is not checked. The impact is limited by the response only exposing len(r.text), which gives a blind or oracle-style SSRF. It still allows internal port and service probing, and content-length inference.

trace.note: url taken directly from the request query string
host.endswith('example.com') is the only validation; it has no dot boundary, and the unused ALLOWED_SUFFIX holds the intended '.example.com'
c.get(url) requests the original attacker-supplied URL
len(r.text) is returned to the caller, so reachability and size of the internal response leak

finding.guards_checked: Hostname suffix check at mirror.py:13 is bypassable via a domain like 'attackerexample.com'. There is no allowlist of exact hosts, no scheme or port restriction, and no DNS-resolution or IP-range blocking (private, loopback and link-local are not blocked). No authentication on the endpoint. httpx does not follow redirects by default, so redirect-based bypass does not apply, but DNS-based bypass does. /ping (mirror.py:23) uses a hardcoded URL and is not vulnerable.

verdict.guard_found: mirror.py:13 host.endswith("example.com") — suffix check without dot boundary; ALLOWED_SUFFIX at line 7 is unused. No scheme/port restriction, no IP check, no auth.
verdict.reason: The `url` query param (mirror.py:11) reaches httpx `c.get(url)` (mirror.py:16) guarded only by the bypassable `endswith("example.com")` at mirror.py:13, and `len(r.text)` is returned at mirror.py:17.
